evidence.note: Built reusable inspection/verification tooling early and mid-run: an AST dumper, a diff tool comparing actual vs expected, and a semantic-token-context dumper — scaffolding reused across many methods to localize faults.

Consistently ran per-method/per-file targeted tests immediately after each change (selectionRange, folding, documentSymbol, references/highlight, callhierarchy, typeDefinition), isolating verification to one handler at a time rather than only the full suite.

Performed case-level, entry/byte-level diffs of its output vs golden (per-entry symbol comparison, fCost output-vs-golden exact ranges, codeLens diff), pinpointing failures to specific cases and fields.
Categorized failures by type/subcategory to direct debugging, treating the aggregate as decomposable signal rather than opaque pass/fail.

Checked for regressions and verified reverts (record hover regressions, references regressions, verify revert, baseline after revert) — guarding against fixes breaking prior passes, though done manually/periodically rather than as automated infrastructure.
Ran the full golden suite periodically as the aggregate checkpoint between focused method-level work — the coarse check layered on top of granular verification.

reasoning: The agent built reusable verification scaffolding (AST/token dumpers, a diff tool), ran per-method harnesses after essentially every change, and performed entry/byte-level actual-vs-golden diffs plus failure categorization to pinpoint faults to a layer and case — squarely the level-8 anchor. It also did regression checks and revert-verification, but these were manual and periodic rather than an automated, continuously-enforced regression-guarding loop, and there is no explicit validation that passes stem from genuine AST analysis vs coincidence, so it stops short of 10.
